points.description: States that the best-case number of operations for insertion sort is N (linear, O(N)), where N is the length of the array.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if says linear/O(N) or N but does not define N as the array length.

points.description: States that the best case occurs when the array is already sorted (in the desired order).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if says nearly sorted or ordered without clearly stating already sorted.

points.description: Correctly links the two: only one comparison per element and no shifting is needed on a sorted array, hence N operations; distinguishes from worst case (reverse-sorted, N^2).

rubric.notes: Full marks need both facts stated precisely: N (linear) operations, N being the array length, and the case being an already sorted array. Give part marks only where over half of a point is precise. A wrong complexity (e.g. N^2, log N) or a wrong scenario (e.g. reverse sorted, random) gets zero for that point. Vague answers such as "it is fast" earn nothing.
